Ekegusii: Ekero Yeremia akoorete goteebia abanto bonsi amang'ana ayio Omonene, Nyasae obo, amotomete kobateebia,

English: I call to You; save me, that I may keep Your testimonies.
Kiswahili: Ninakuita; niokoe nami nitazishika sheria zako.
Ekegusii: Nigo ’nkorera asore, ontoorie, erinde ’mbwate oborori bwao.

English: Now the islands will tremble in the day of your fall. Yes, the islands that are in the sea will be dismayed at your departure.'
Kiswahili: Sasa nchi za pwani zinatetemeka katika siku ya anguko lako; visiwa vilivyomo baharini vinaogopa kwa kuporomoka kwako.'
Ekegusii: Bono ebisinka mbiiguswe ase rituko ri'ogokwa kwao, ee, ebisinka bire ase enyancha mbigoichanere ekero orasirigwe.

English: what He did for you in the wilderness until you reached this place;
Kiswahili: Sio watoto wenu walioyaona yale Mungu aliyowafanyia huko jangwani mpaka mkafika mahali hapa,
Ekegusii: ’Momanyete buna Omonene abakorerete, ekero mwarenge ase erooro, goika mogaacha aase aa.

English: Direct me in the path of your commandments, for I delight in them.
Kiswahili: Niongoze kwenye njia ya amri zako, kwa kuwa huko napata furaha.
Ekegusii: Indaae 'mbwatie enchera y'amachiiko ao, ekiagera inche nigo 'ngokirie naro.

English: Kiriath Baal (also called Kiriath Jearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages.
Kiswahili: Kiriath-Baali (yaani Kiriath-Yearimu) na Raba; miji miwili pamoja na vijiji vyake.
Ekegusii: Naende yarengeo Kiriati‐Baali (noro Kiriati‐Yearimu), na Raba, emechie ebere, amo nebichie biabo.

English: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
Kiswahili: “Kama fahali wa mtu fulani atamuumiza fahali wa mtu mwingine na akafa, watamuuza yule aliye hai na wagawane sawa fedha pamoja na mnyama aliyekufa.
Ekegusii: Eeri y’omonto keraite ey’omonto onde ekwe, erio barabwo baoonie eeri eyio ere moyo, baatanane chitaabu echio, baatanane ne chinyama chi’eng’ombe eria y akuure boigo.

English: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died
Kiswahili: Wakati Zimri alipoona kuwa mji umechukuliwa, alikwenda ndani ya ngome ya jumba la kifalme na kulichoma moto jumba la kifalme na kujiteketeza ndani yake. Kwa hiyo akafa,
Ekegusii: Ekero Simuri aroche ng’a omochie obwatirwe, agasoa ase eburi y’enyomba y’omorwoti, agasamba enyomba y’omorwoti, na Simuri omonyene agesamberao.

English: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
Kiswahili: Elihorefu na Ahiya, wana wa Shisha: waandishi; Yehoshafati mwana wa Ahiludi: karani;
Ekegusii: Elihorefu na Ahiya, basinto ba Sisa, nabwo baarenge abariki. Yehosafati, mosinto bw’Ahiludi, nere orenge omoriki bw’amang’ana are gokoreka.

English: Jehu met some relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and asked, “Who are you?” “We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered, “and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and of the queen mother.”
Kiswahili: Yehu akakutana na watu wa jamaa ya Ahazia mfalme wa Yuda, akauliza, “Ninyi ni nani?” Wao wakasema, “Sisi ni jamaa ya Ahazia, nasi tumeshuka kuwasalimu jamaa ya mfalme na ya mama malkia.”
Ekegusii: akaumerana nabamwabo Ahasia, omorwoti bw’Abayuda, akabooria: “Inwe mbarabi?” Nabarabwo bakairaneria: “Intwe nigo tore abamwabo Ahasia, nigo tokogenda gokwania abana b’omorwoti, na ab’eting’ana, ng’ina omorwoti.”

English: There was not a man left in Ai or Bethel who didn't go out after Israel. They left the city open, and pursued Israel.
Kiswahili: Hakuna hata mwanaume mmoja aliyebakia Ai wala Betheli ambaye hakufuatia Israeli. Wakauacha mji wazi na kuwafuatia Israeli.
Ekegusii: Kera omonto agatiga omochie ase okobwatia Abaisraeli. Onde tatigarete ime ya Ai, gose Beteli; omochie ogatigwa bosa otari na getango.

English: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars;
Kiswahili: makomamanga 400 kwa ajili ya hizo nyavu mbili (safu mbili za makomamanga kwa kila wavu, yakipamba hayo mataji mawili yenye umbo la bakuli juu ya hizo nguzo);
Ekegusii: na emegwekano y'amakomomanga amagana ane eyabegetwe igoro y'ebichanga ebio, chindwaro ibere ase kera egesure kiarenge igoro ye chisiiro, erinde ensemo y'ebisure biria yatambeete etubwe.

English: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
Kiswahili: Baadaye kidogo, mtu mwingine alimwona Petro akasema, “Wewe pia ni mmoja wao!” Petro akajibu, “Wewe mtu, mimi sio mmoja wao!”
Ekegusii: Naende ake omonto onde akamorora, akabora, “Aye noyomo obo ore.” Petero akabora, “Omonto oyo, tai inche.”

English: No sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten. It shall be burned with fire.
Kiswahili: Lakini kila sadaka ya dhambi ambayo damu yake imeletwa ndani ya Hema la Kukutania kufanya upatanisho katika Mahali Patakatifu kamwe haitaliwa; lazima iteketezwe.
Ekegusii: Korende ekeng'wanso ki'ebibe, ekio amanyinga aye araarentwe ime y'Eema y'Omosangererekano ase ogokora okobwatanigwa ime y'Aase Aachenu tigekoriegwa, nigo kerasambwe n'omorero.

English: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
Kiswahili: Wanakufa ghafula, usiku wa manane; watu wanatikiswa nao hupita; wenye nguvu huondolewa bila mkono wa mwanadamu.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo bagokwa ara rimo; nigo bakonyegerigwa botuko gati, basira kegima, baria bare nokobua nigo bagosirigwa ko tari namaboko a Mwanyabaanto.

English: The name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the captain of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
Kiswahili: Jina la mkewe Sauli aliitwa Ahinoamu binti wa Ahimaasi. Jina la jemadari wa jeshi la Sauli aliitwa Abneri mwana wa Neri, naye Neri alikuwa babaye mdogo Sauli.
Ekegusii: Moga Saulo nigo areenge korokwa Ahinoamu omosubati bw'Ahimasi. Omochiki bw'abarwani b'esegi nigo areenge korokwa Abineri, mosinto o Neri, oyorenge ise moke Saulo.

English: You shall put it on a lace of blue, and it shall be on the sash. It shall be on the front of the sash.
Kiswahili: Lifunge hilo bamba kwa kamba ya buluu kwenye kilemba, nalo ni lazima liwe mbele ya kilemba.
Ekegusii: Oyesiberanie bosio bw'ekegogwa ne chiusi chire buru.

English: You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left few in number, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God.
Kiswahili: Ninyi ambao mlikuwa wengi kama nyota za angani mtaachwa wachache tu, kwa sababu hamkumtii Bwana Mungu wenu.
Ekegusii: Nonya more abange buna ching’enang’eni chia igoro, ’namosirigwe motigare more abake mono, ekiagera motaigwerete Omonene Nyasae oino.

English: You shall remember all the way which Yahweh your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.
Kiswahili: Kumbuka jinsi Bwana Mungu wenu alivyowaongoza katika njia yote katika jangwa kwa miaka hii arobaini, kukunyenyekeza na kukujaribu ili ajue lililoko moyoni mwako, kwamba utayashika maagizo yake au la.
Ekegusii: Moinyore buna Omonene Nyasae oino, abeire okobaraa ase orogeendo rwaino rwonsi ase erooro, ase engaki y'emiaka emerongo ene yaetire, ase okobakora mobe abaitongo na kobateema ase okomanya ebirengerio biaino, arore gose 'moganetie korenda amachiiko aye, gose yaya.

English: A mixed race will occupy Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
Kiswahili: Wageni watakalia mji wa Ashdodi, nami nitakatilia mbali kiburi cha Wafilisti.
Ekegusii: Asidodi nomenywe nabaanto batarochi inchera, na inche Omonene ninsirie kegima oboenenu bw’Abafilisti.

English: I have seen the wicked in great power, spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil.
Kiswahili: Nimemwona mtu mwovu na mkatili akistawi kama mwerezi wa Lebanoni,
Ekegusii: Narorire omokori amabe otindire ase obomwenu, akaba okoranda buna emecharake egokina ase amaroba amatobu.

English: Every city flees at the sound of the horseman and archer. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no inhabitant is left.
Kiswahili: Kwa sauti ya wapanda farasi na wapiga upinde kila mji unakimbia. Baadhi wanakimbilia vichakani, baadhi wanapanda juu ya miamba. Miji yote imeachwa, hakuna aishiye ndani yake.
Ekegusii: Abanto ba kera omochie mbatame ekero baraigwe amariogi ’abariini chibarasi na ay’abwo babwate amata, mbatame gochia ase amanani, bebise ase ebitare ime. Emechie yonsi netigare bosa, nonya nomonto oyomo tagotigara aroro.

English: I have come in my Father's name, and you don't receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
Kiswahili: Mimi nimekuja kwa jina la Baba yangu, nanyi hamnipokei, lakini mtu mwingine akija kwa jina lake mwenyewe, mtampokea.
Ekegusii: Inche nachire ase erieta ria Tata one, na inwe timori konyancha; oyonde karaache ase erieta riaye omonyene, oyio namomwanche.

English: But Naaman insisted, “Please, take two talents.” And he urged Gehazi to accept them. Then he tied up two talents of silver in two bags along with two sets of clothing and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
Kiswahili: Naamani akasema, “Hakika, chukua talanta mbili za fedha.” Akamsihi Gehazi azipokee, kisha akafunga talanta mbili za fedha katika mifuko miwili pamoja na mivao miwili ya mavazi. Akawapa watumishi wake wawili mizigo hiyo, nao wakaibeba wakitangulia mbele ya Gehazi.
Ekegusii: Naamani akamoteebia: “Koranche oire chitalanta ibere.” Igo akamosorora, akamosibera chitalanta ibere chi’echifeta ase emebuko ebere, akamoa ne chianga ibere, agatweka abasomba baye babere. Barabwo bakabibogoria, bagatang’ana bosio bwa Gehasi.

English: David counted the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
Kiswahili: Daudi akakusanya watu aliokuwa nao na kuweka majemadari wa maelfu na majemadari wa mamia.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Daudi akaroberia abanto baye, akabaatanana ase ebiombe bi'elifu elifu, na ebie rigana, akababeekera abatang'ani

English: This man will be punished in the streets of the city. He will be seized where he least expects it.
Kiswahili: Mtu huyu ataadhibiwa katika mitaa ya jiji. Atakamatwa mahali ambapo hatarajii.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio omonyabibe ere nabwatwe engaki eria atakagereti na koegwa egesusuro ase obosio bwa abanto bonsi.

English: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
Kiswahili: Ndipo wakatafuta kumkamata, lakini hakuna mtu yeyote aliyethubutu kumshika kwa sababu saa yake ilikuwa bado haijawadia.
Ekegusii: Igo bakarigia komobwata, korende onde tari oramborete okoboko kwaye, erinde amobwate, ekiagera ensa yaye konya teraika.

English: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.
Kiswahili: Wanafunzi wake walipomwona akitembea juu ya maji, waliingiwa na hofu kuu, wakasema, “Ni mzimu.” Wakapiga yowe kwa kuogopa.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero aborokigwa bachia komorora ogotaara ase enyancha igoro, bakaondoka, bakaboora, “Eri nerirengari!” Bagaaka eriogi ase okoiroka.

English: for, to comfort them, quails came up for them from the sea.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana, ili kuwafariji, kware walitoka baharini kwa ajili yao.
Ekegusii: Ekero baganetie endagera egwansa mono, bakaegwa chikware korwa roche echio bariete buna endagera.

English: The archers have severely grieved him, shot at him, and persecuted him:
Kiswahili: Kwa uchungu wapiga mshale walimshambulia, wakampiga mshale kwa ukatili.
Ekegusii: Abaruti emegwe bakomoimokera ase okomogwera n'bororo, bakomoruta emegwe na komoorosia,

English: “‘“There will no longer be a pricking brier to the house of Israel, nor a hurting thorn of any that are around them that scorned them. Then they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”
Kiswahili: “ ‘Nyumba ya Israeli hawatakuwa tena na majirani wenye nia ya kuwadhuru wanaoumiza kama michongoma na miiba mikali. Ndipo watakapojua kwamba Mimi ndimi Bwana Mwenyezi.
Ekegusii: “Korende ase Abaisraeli, chimbambo gose amagwa tibikobao bibabete ekero bagendererete komenya ase egati y' abanto abwo baabaetanaine baabachaayete. Erio mbamanye ng'a inche ninche Omonene.

English: Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo, msiwaoze binti zenu kwa wana wao wala binti zao kwa wana wenu. Msitafute mkataba wa urafiki nao kwa wakati wowote. Ndipo mtakapofanikiwa na kula mema ya nchi na kuwaachia watoto wenu nchi hiyo kama urithi wao wa milele.’
Ekegusii: Ase ayio, timobaisa gosokia abaiseke baino ase abamura babo, gose timobaisa kobarigeria omorembe gose ogosesenigwa. Mobe abakong’u na morie amaya ay’ense eye na moyetigere abana baino ebe omwando obo kogenderera botambe.

English: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done.
Kiswahili: Akafanya yaliyo mema machoni pa Bwana, kama Uzia baba yake alivyokuwa amefanya.
Ekegusii: Ere agakora ayare amaronge ase amaiso ’Omonene, buna aya onsi Usia ise akorete.

English: He said to him, “Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers, and well with the flock; and bring me word again.” So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo akamwambia, “Nenda uone kama mambo yote ni salama kwa ndugu zako na makundi, kisha uniletee habari.” Ndipo akamtuma Yosefu kutoka Bonde la Hebroni. Yosefu alipofika Shekemu,
Ekegusii: Ise akamoteebia: “Genda bono orore gose abamino mbuya bare amo namaicho, erinde ondetere amang'ana.” Ase igo, akamotoma korwa ase omweya o Heburoni, akageenda agaika Sekemu;

English: All these men had married foreign women, and some of them had children by these wives.
Kiswahili: Hawa wote walikuwa wameoa wanawake wa kigeni, na baadhi yao walikuwa wamezaa nao watoto.
Ekegusii: Abanto aba bonsi konya banyuomire abakungu b’ebisaku ebiao, na abande b’abwo konya baiboire abana.

English: I will make Pathros desolate, and will set a fire in Zoan, and will execute judgments on No.
Kiswahili: Nitaifanya Pathrosi kuwa ukiwa na kuitia moto Soani, nami nitaipiga kwa adhabu Thebesi
Ekegusii: Ninsarie ense ya Patirosi esire ebe bosa, ninsambe Soani nomorero, na inachere omochie okorokwa No ekiina.

English: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who has led me to Edom?
Kiswahili: Ni nani atakayenipeleka hadi mji wenye ngome? Ni nani atakayeniongoza hadi nifike Edomu?
Ekegusii: Ning'o orandaae ansoyie ase omochie ogiteire chindwaki? Ning'o orantang'ane gochia Edomu?

English: Show your marvelous loving kindness, you who save those who take refuge by your right hand from their enemies.
Kiswahili: Uonyeshe ajabu ya upendo wako mkuu, wewe uokoaye kwa mkono wako wa kuume wale wanaokukimbilia kutokana na adui zao.
Ekegusii: Aye Omotooria bw'abagotamera okoboko kwao kwa borio korwa ase ababisa babo, oorokia obwanchani bwao bw'ogokumia.

English: ‘Cursed is he who sleeps with his mother-in-law.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
Kiswahili: “Alaaniwe mtu akutanaye kimwili na mama mkwe wake.” Kisha watu wote watasema, “Amen!”
Ekegusii: “Aragererigwe omonto oraraare na ng’ina biara. “Abanto bonsi bairanerie, bateebe: Amina.

English: The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
Kiswahili: Wakati wowote upinde wa mvua unapotokea mawinguni, nitauona na kukumbuka Agano la milele kati ya Mungu na viumbe vyote vilivyo hai vya kila aina duniani.”
Ekegusii: Ekero omokubinyongo okoba ase amare, na inche nkoyorigereria, ning'inyore okobwatana kwane gwa kare na kare, okwo nakorire egati yane, buna inche Nyasae na kera egetongwa kere moyo ase ense.”

English: who say, “Let him make haste, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”
Kiswahili: kwa wale wanaosema, “Mungu na afanye haraka, aharakishe kazi yake ili tupate kuiona. Huo mpango wa Aliye Mtakatifu wa Israeli na ukamilike, tena udhihirike ili tupate kuujua.”
Ekegusii: bateeba, “Tiga Omonene ache bwango, aayererie emeremo yaye, erinde toyerore. Tiga aya Oyore Omochenu bw'Abaisraeli aroberetie asuke gocha ang'e aikerane, erio nario toranyare koyamanya.”

English: Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn't understand what he was telling them.
Kiswahili: Yesu alitumia mfano huu, lakini wao hawakuelewa hayo aliyokuwa akiwaambia.
Ekegusii: Omoreng'anio oyo Yeso akabateebia, korende barabwo tibamanyete amang'ana ayio abateebeetie.

English: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”
Kiswahili: “Vivyo hivyo, wa mwisho watakuwa wa kwanza, na wa kwanza watakuwa wa mwisho.”
Ekegusii: Naboigo abamagega inababe ab'eritang'ani, na ab'eritang'ani inababe abamagega.”

English: For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa mwana humdharau baba yake, naye binti huinuka dhidi ya mama yake, mkwe kuwa kinyume na mama mkwe wake: adui wa mtu ni wale wa nyumbani mwake hasa.
Ekegusii: Omwana omomura nigo agochaaya ise, na omwana omoiseke nigo akoamererania na ng'ina, na moka momura oamererania na ng'ina biara. Ababisa b'omonto nabaanto b'enyomba yaye omonyene.

English: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
Kiswahili: siku ile walinzi wa nyumba watakapotetemeka, nao watu wenye nguvu watakapojiinamisha, wakati wasagao watakapokoma kwa sababu ya uchache, nao wachunguliao madirishani kutiwa giza;
Ekegusii: Engaki eyio abarendi b'enyomba mbaiguswe, na abasacha bare ne chinguru bekumbe, na abagosia batige gosia ekiagera bare abake ase omobaro, na abwo batengerete korwa ase ebibao, batubwe norotutu tibarora buya.

English: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
Kiswahili: Ndipo wanafunzi wake wote wakamwacha, wakakimbia.
Ekegusii: Erio aborokigwa bonsi bakamotiga, bagatama. Omomura oyotamete

English: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”
Kiswahili: Niliwaambia kuwa mtakufa katika dhambi zenu, kwa maana msipoamini ya kwamba ‘Mimi Ndiye,’ mtakufa katika dhambi zenu.”
Ekegusii: Ase ayio nabateebia ng’a namokwe ase ebibe biaino. Onye timokwegena ng’a inche nere, namokwe ase ebibe biaino.”

English: Listen to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last.
Kiswahili: “Ee Yakobo, nisikilize mimi, Israeli, ambaye nimekuita: Mimi ndiye; mimi ndimi mwanzo na mwisho.
Ekegusii: “Inwe ab’ororeeria rwa Yakobo, inwe Abaisraeli, aba narangeretie, ntegerere! Inche ninche Ere, ninche omochakano na omoerio.

English: He was like the morning star among clouds, like the full moon,
Kiswahili: Alikuwa kama nyota ya asubuhi katikati ya mawingu, kama mwezi mpevu,
Ekegusii: Ere nigo arenge buna eng'enang'eni ya mambia ere ase amare, nigo arenge buna omotienyi orabete.

English: A wicked man hardens his face; but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwovu ana uso wa ushupavu, bali mtu mnyofu huzifikiria njia zake.
Ekegusii: Omokori amabe nigo agokong'ia obosio bwaye, korende oyore nenkoro endonge nigo akorenda orogendo rw'aye.

English: Yahweh did so; and there came grievous swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants' houses. In all the land of Egypt the land was corrupted by reason of the swarms of flies.
Kiswahili: Naye Bwana akafanya hivyo. Makundi makubwa ya mainzi yalimiminika katika jumba la kifalme la Farao na katika nyumba za maafisa wake, pia nchi yote ya Misri ikaharibiwa na mainzi.
Ekegusii: Omonene agakora ayio. Chingi chigaacha ase obonge mono ase chinyomba chia Farao, na echi'abasomba baye, na ase ense yonsi ya Misiri. Na ense eria egasarigwa ne chingi chiria.

English: Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
Kiswahili: Enyi watawala, je, kweli mwanena kwa haki? Je, mnahukumu kwa unyofu miongoni mwa watu?
Ekegusii: Inwe abamokogamba, Inee, ngokwana more amang’ana ’ekeene? Inee! Nkonachera more abanto ebiina bire boronge?

English: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws, which Yahweh made between him and the children of Israel in Mount Sinai by Moses.
Kiswahili: Hizi ndizo amri, sheria na pia masharti ambazo Bwana alifanya kati yake mwenyewe na Waisraeli katika Mlima Sinai kupitia kwa Mose.
Ekegusii: Eyio nero emeroberio echiikire amo namachiik'Omonene aruete goetera ase omonwa o Musa, agwo ase egetunwa gia Sinai, ebe ase egati yaye na Abaisraeli.

English: He was with them hidden in God's house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.
Kiswahili: Alibaki amefichwa pamoja nao katika Hekalu la Mungu kwa muda wa miaka sita wakati Athalia alikuwa akitawala nchi.
Ekegusii: Yoashi akaba amo nabarabwo ase emiaka etano nomo, abisire ase enyomba ya Nyasae, ekero Atalia arenge kogamba igoro ase ense eria.

English: Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the LORD protects the city, its watchmen stand guard in vain.
Kiswahili: Bwana asipoijenga nyumba, wajengao hufanya kazi bure. Bwana asipoulinda mji, walinzi wakesha bure.
Ekegusii: Onye Omonene takoagaacha enyomba, abwo bakoyeagaacha nigo bagokora emeremo ya bosa. Onye Omonene takorenda omochie omonto oyio okoyorenda nigo akorenda bosa.

English: The Lord Yahweh says: “I will spread out my net on you with a company of many peoples. They will bring you up in my net.
Kiswahili: “ ‘Hili ndilo Bwana Mwenyezi asemalo: “ ‘Nikiwa pamoja na wingi mkubwa wa watu nitautupa wavu wangu juu yako, nao watakukokota katika wavu wangu.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio, aya naro Omonene agoteeba: Nindute ekeonga kiane igoro yao, nakio omoganda omonene orakong'use okobeke ase rikuru riane ime.

English: Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, and he didn't see the king's face.
Kiswahili: Absalomu akaishi miaka miwili huko Yerusalemu pasipo kuuona uso wa mfalme.
Ekegusii: Abisalomu akamenya Yerusalemu emiaka ebere atana gochia kororana nomorwoti.

English: Behold, the Lord will dispossess her, and he will strike her power in the sea; and she will be devoured with fire.
Kiswahili: Lakini Bwana atamwondolea mali zake na kuuangamiza uwezo wake wa baharini, naye atateketezwa kwa moto.
Ekegusii: Korende rora, Omonene nayoure chinibo chiaye, na atugute okobua kwaye ase enyancha, na omochie oyio omonyene nosambwe nomorero.

English: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls out from the heights of the city.
Kiswahili: Amewatuma watumishi wake wa kike, naye huita kutoka mahali pa juu sana pa mji.
Ekegusii: Bwatomire abasomba baye abaiseke gochia aase aimokererete igoro mono yomochie korangeria abanto, bogoteeba:

English: Speak, “Yahweh says, “‘The dead bodies of men will fall as dung on the open field, and as the handful after the harvester. No one will gather them.'”
Kiswahili: Sema, “Hili ndilo asemalo Bwana: “ ‘Maiti za wanaume zitalala kama mavi katika mashamba, kama malundo ya nafaka nyuma ya mvunaji, wala hakuna anayekusanya.' ”
Ekegusii: Kwana: “Aya nar'Omonene agoteeba: Abanto mbakwe, na emebere yabo esiarerwe aande onsi, ebe buna esike ase emegondo, na buna emesaima yatigetwe nabagesi, onde takoyesangereria.”

English: When the cloud stayed on the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel kept Yahweh's command, and didn't travel.
Kiswahili: Wakati wingu lilipobaki juu ya Maskani kwa muda mrefu, Waisraeli walitii amri ya Bwana nao hawakuondoka.
Ekegusii: Onye riire riria riarenge kobeera igoro ase Obomenyo boria amatuko amaange, Abaisraeli nigo baigwerete Omonene, na barabwo tibarenge komanora kogeenda.

English: For he fashioned the two pillars of bronze, eighteen cubits high apiece; and a line of twelve cubits encircled either of them.
Kiswahili: Hiramu akasubu nguzo mbili za shaba, kila moja ikiwa na urefu wa dhiraa kumi na nane, kila nguzo ikiwa na mzingo wa dhiraa kumi na mbili kwa mstari.
Ekegusii: Hiramu akaroisia chisiiro ibere chi'etai; obotambe bwa kera esiiro eyemo nigo bwareenge obw'amaboko ikomi na atato, na engori y'obotambe bw'amaboko ikomi na abere egaetanana kera esiiro.

English: “Son of man, take up a lament for the king of Tyre and tell him that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.
Kiswahili: “Mwanadamu, mfanyie maombolezo mfalme wa Tiro, nawe umwambie: ‘Hili ndilo Bwana Mwenyezi asemalo: “ ‘Ulikuwa kipeo cha ukamilifu, ukiwa umejaa hekima na mkamilifu katika uzuri.
Ekegusii: “Aye Mwanyabaanto, bokia amagombo igoro y’omorwoti o Turo, omoteebie ng’a aya naro Omonene agoteeba: Aye nigo kwarenge omoikeranu goetania ebitongwa bionsi bi’obonene; nigo gwaichire nobong’aini, naende kwarenge omosiani omoikeranu.

English: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers marched up toward Israel. And when the Israelites learned of this, they feared the Philistines
Kiswahili: Wafilisti waliposikia kwamba Israeli wamekusanyika huko Mispa, watawala wa Wafilisti wakapanda ili kuwashambulia. Waisraeli waliposikia habari hiyo, waliogopa kwa sababu ya Wafilisti.
Ekegusii: Ekero Abafirisiti baigwete ng’a Abaisraeli basangererekanire agwo Misipa, abanene b’Abafilisti bakagenda gochia kobarwania. Abaisraeli bagachia koigwa amang’ana ayio, bakabairoka,

English: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
Kiswahili: Wakati nchi inapoangukia mikononi mwa waovu, yeye huwafunga macho mahakimu wake. Kama si yeye, basi ni nani?
Ekegusii: Ense nigo ebeekire inse y’amaboko ’abakori amabe, Nyasae otubire amasio ’abagaambi ebiina. Onye tari ere, ning’o rende okorire ayio?

English: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
Kiswahili: Maneno ya kupendeza ni kama sega la asali, ni matamu kwa nafsi na uponyaji kwenye mifupa.
Ekegusii: Amang'ana y'okogokia nigo anga obooke bokorwa ase richoe, nigo are amansu ase omoyo naende nigo akogwenia omobere.

English: God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
Kiswahili: Mungu akaibariki siku ya saba akaifanya takatifu, kwa sababu katika siku hiyo alipumzika kutoka kazi zote za kuumba alizokuwa amefanya.
Ekegusii: Nyasae agasesenia rituko ria gatano na kabere, akariatanana, akarikora richenu, ekiagera erio nario rituko atimogete korwa ase emeremo yaye yonsi y'obotongi, eyio konya akorire.

English: Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”
Kiswahili: Wamewaoa baadhi ya binti zao kuwa wake zao na wake za wana wao, nao wamechanganya taifa takatifu na watu waliowazunguka. Nao viongozi na maafisa wamekuwa mstari wa mbele katika njia hii potovu.”
Ekegusii: Barabwo banyuomire abaiseke b’abaanto abwo, naende banyuomeirie abamura babo abaiseke b’abaanto abwo. Bono egesaku eke egechenu giochoganire nabaanto b’echinse echi. Abagaambi na abatang’ani b’abaanto nabwo bare ab’eritang’ani ase ogokora okwo kw’ogotegenwa.”

English: The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you.”
Kiswahili: Fimbo ya mtu nitakayemchagua itachipuka, nami mwenyewe nitayakomesha haya manungʼuniko ya mara kwa mara ya Waisraeli dhidi yako.”
Ekegusii: Enyimbo y’omonto oria inche ’ndachoore neseboke. Ase enchera eyio ninkore Abaisraeli batige kwemurungania mamincha y’ane, naende ningere batige kwemurungania mamincha yaino.”

English: He looked, and saw a well in the field, and saw three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well's mouth was large.
Kiswahili: Huko akaona kisima katika shamba, pamoja na makundi matatu ya kondoo yamelala karibu na kisima hicho kwa sababu walikuwa wanakunywa maji kutoka kwenye kisimani hicho. Jiwe lililokuwa mdomoni mwa kisima lilikuwa kubwa.
Ekegusii: Agwo akarigereria akarora ensoko yaare ase egetii, na amaicho atato e ching'ondi araire ensoko eyio ensemo, ekiagera ase ensoko eyio nao amaicho are konywera amaache. Na ndiareenge aroro rigena rinene igoro y'omonwa bw'ensoko.

English: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?
Kiswahili: Ilipofika siku ya Sabato, akaanza kufundisha katika sinagogi, na wengi waliomsikia wakashangaa. Nao wakauliza, “Mtu huyu ameyapata wapi mambo haya yote? Tazama ni hekima ya namna gani hii aliyopewa? Tazama matendo ya miujiza ayafanyayo kwa mikono yake!
Ekegusii: Na ekero gi’Esabato agachaaka kworokereria ase esinagogi; abange abamoigwete bagakumia, bagateebania, “Oyo ng’ai anyorire aya? Mbong’aini ki obo aeirwe oyo? Ogokora gwe chinguru ki oko okonene kogokoreka ase amaboko aye?

English: “Son of man, set your face against Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel
Kiswahili: “Mwanadamu, uelekeze uso wako juu ya Yerusalemu na uhubiri dhidi ya mahali patakatifu. Tabiri dhidi ya nchi ya Israeli
Ekegusii: “Aye Mwanyabaanto, rigereria gochia Yerusalemu, orarie ring’ana rire mamincha y’Aase Aachenu, na obaane mamincha y’ense y’Abaisraeli.

English: Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go through the land, to all the springs of water, and to all the brooks. Perhaps we may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, that we not lose all the animals.”
Kiswahili: Ahabu alikuwa amemwambia Obadia, “Nenda katika nchi yote kwenye vijito vyote na mabonde. Huenda tunaweza kupata majani ya kuwalisha farasi na nyumbu wapate kuishi ili tusilazimike kuwaua hata mmoja wa wanyama wetu.”
Ekegusii: Ahabu agateebia Obadia: “Togende toete ase ense yonsi na ase chinsoko chi'amaache, na ase amagooko onsi; ande nabo torabaise konyora obonyansi, erinde totoorie chibarasi ne chibarasi chibe moyo, na titobaisa gosiria chitugo chinde.”

English: A Psalm by David. Hear my prayer, Yahweh. Listen to my petitions. In your faithfulness and righteousness, relieve me.
Kiswahili: Zaburi ya Daudi. Ee Bwana, sikia sala yangu, sikiliza kilio changu unihurumie; katika uaminifu na haki yako njoo unisaidie.
Ekegusii: (Ogoteera gwa Daudi) Aye Omonene, oigwe ogosaba kwane; ase engencho y'oboronge bwao otegerere ogosorora kwane, ong'iranerie ase engencho y'obwegenwa bwao.

English: If a man finds a lady who is a virgin, who is not pledged to be married, grabs her and lies with her, and they are found,
Kiswahili: Ikiwa itatokea mwanaume akutane na bikira ambaye hajaposwa na kumbaka nao wakakutwa,
Ekegusii: “Omonto karaumerane n'omoiseke omwekungi otararierwa boko, na komobwata ne chinguru, abe nere, nabarabwo babere banyorwe,

English: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.
Kiswahili: Vivyo hivyo, myaonapo mambo haya yote, mnatambua kwamba wakati u karibu, hata malangoni.
Ekegusii: Naboigo nainwe komokorora aya aorokire, momanye ng’a omoerio obeire ang’e na gesieri.

English: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Sidonians, tranquil and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Sidonians and had no alliance with anyone.
Kiswahili: Basi hao watu watano wakaondoka na kufika Laishi, mahali ambapo waliwakuta watu wanaishi salama, kama Wasidoni, kwa utulivu na bila mashaka. Nchi yao haikupungukiwa na kitu chochote, hivyo wakawa tajiri. Pia walikaa mbali sana na Wasidoni, wala hawakushughulika na mtu yeyote.
Ekegusii: Erio abanto baria batano bakarua aroro, bakageenda goika omochie o Laisi. Na agwo bakarora buna abanto bamenyete bare n’obogima botari n’obwoba, buna abanto ba Sidoni. Nigo barenge abanto abatoereru na ab’omorembe, bataremeiri gento korwa ase riroba. Nigo bamenyete are korwa ase Abasidoni, naende tibarenge gosanga n’abanto bande.

English: He carved all the walls of the house around with carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, inside and outside.
Kiswahili: Juu ya kuta zote zilizozunguka Hekalu, za vyumba vya ndani na vya nje, zilipambwa kwa nakshi zilizokatwa za makerubi, miti ya mitende na maua yaliyochanua.
Ekegusii: Sulemani agachabera chinyasi chionsi chie Hekalu, na echi'akanyomba ka ime, nemegwekano y'ebitongwa bibwate chimbaba, na ey'emekendo, na ey'ebisicha, yabaachetwe ase chibao echio.

English: He rained down manna on them to eat, and gave them food from the sky.
Kiswahili: akawanyeshea mana ili watu wale; aliwapa nafaka ya mbinguni.
Ekegusii: akabatweria endagera ekorokwa mana, bakaba bakoyeria; ee, akabaa endagera korwa igoro.

English: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.’”
Kiswahili: Samaki waliomo katika Mto Naili watakufa, nao mto utanuka vibaya, Wamisri hawataweza kunywa hayo maji yake.’ ”
Ekegusii: Ne chinswe chire ase orooche ime inachikwe, chigunde, na orooche narotioke bobe, na Abamisiri nabasinywe konywa amaache aria.”

English: When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, and were very afraid.
Kiswahili: Wanafunzi waliposikia haya, wakaanguka chini kifudifudi, wakajawa na hofu.
Ekegusii: Ekero aborokigwa bachia koigwa aya, bakagwa inse maumama, bakabwatwa nomoondoko omonene.

English: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
Kiswahili: Yesu akamjibu, “Mbona unaniita mwema? Hakuna yeyote aliye mwema ila Mungu peke yake.
Ekegusii: Yeso akamoiraneria, “Naki okondoka omuya? Onde tari omuya otatiga Nyasae bweka.

English: The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the one to be cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Kiswahili: Kuhani atakayemtangaza kuwa safi atahitaji kumkabidhi mgonjwa aliyepona pamoja na sadaka zake zote mbele za Bwana katika ingilio la Hema la Kukutania.
Ekegusii: Omokuani otenenerete arente omonto oria ogochia gochenwa amo nokoruegwa okwo ase obosio bwane inche Omonene, agwo ase egesoero ki’Eema y’Omosangererekano.

English: and shall not turn away from any of the words which I command you today, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.
Kiswahili: Usihalifu amri zangu zozote ninazokupa leo, kwa kwenda kuume au kushoto, kwa kufuata miungu mingine na kuitumikia.
Ekegusii: Ayio nigo arakoreke onye timokoonchoka aande, gochia ensemo y'okorio gose ey'okobee, timotiga nonya ne'ring'ana erimo ri'ayio nabaeire ase rituko ria reero, erinde mogeende gosasiima chinyasae ching'ao na gochikorera.

English: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’” Paul the Roman Citizen
Kiswahili: “Ndipo Bwana akaniambia, ‘Nenda, kwa maana nitakutuma mbali, kwa watu wa Mataifa.’ ” Paulo Na Jemadari Wa Kirumi
Ekegusii: Nere aganteebia: Genda, ekiagera inche ningotome aare ase abanto b’Ebisaku.” Paulo ogoteeba ng’a n’Omorumi are

English: Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Kiswahili: Kutoka wazao wa Harimu: Maaseya, Eliya, Shemaya, Yehieli na Uzia.
Ekegusii: abeamate ya Harimu: Maaseya na Elija, Semaya na Yehieli, na Usia;

English: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo Yakobo akatumika miaka saba ili kumpata Raheli, lakini ilionekana kwake kama siku chache tu kwa sababu ya upendo wake kwa Raheli.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, Yakobo akamokorera emiaka etano na ebere aegwe Raeli. Emiaka eyio ekarorekana asare buna namatuko makeigo, ekiagera nigo amwanchete Raeli mono.

English: Clouds and darkness surround Him; righteousness and justice are His throne’s foundation.
Kiswahili: Mawingu na giza nene vinamzunguka, haki na hukumu ndio msingi wa kiti chake cha enzi.
Ekegusii: Amare na omosunte ekerima nigo bimoetanaine; oboronge na ekeene nabio bire oboroso bw’ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene.

English: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
Kiswahili: Lakini watamwitaje yeye ambaye hawajamwamini? Nao watawezaje kumwamini yeye ambaye hawajamsikia? Tena watamsikiaje bila mtu kuwahubiria?
Ekegusii: Inee! Inaki baramorangerie ere bataramwegena? Naende inaki baramwegene oyo batana koigwa amang’ana igoro yaye? Naende inaki baraigwe batari nomorandia?

English: Search in the book of Yahweh, and read: not one of these will be missing. None will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them.
Kiswahili: Angalieni katika gombo la Bwana na msome: Hakuna hata mmoja katika hawa atakayekosekana, hakuna hata mmoja atakayemkosa mwenzi wake. Kwa kuwa ni kinywa chake Mungu kimeagiza, na Roho wake atawakusanya pamoja.
Ekegusii: Rigia korwa ase egetabu y'Omonene, mosome: Nonya nekemo ki'ebitongwa ebio tigekobora kobeera aroro, kera ekemo goika kebe nekiamwabo. Omonene ochikiire amang'ana ayio, na Omoika oye nobisangererieo.

English: If the latter husband hates her, and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house; or if the latter husband dies, who took her to be his wife;
Kiswahili: ikiwa mume wake wa pili atachukizwa naye akamwandikia hati ya talaka, akampa na kumfukuza kutoka nyumbani kwake, au kama akifa,
Ekegusii: na oyo nere amwange, amoriikere riruube ri'ogotigana, amoseerie korwa bwoye, gose omosacha oyio o kabere akwe.

English: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, according as I covenanted with David your father, saying, ‘There shall not fail you a man to be ruler in Israel.'
Kiswahili: Nitakiimarisha kiti chako cha enzi kama nilivyoagana na Daudi baba yako niliposema, ‘Hutakosa kamwe mtu wa kutawala juu ya Israeli.'
Ekegusii: rirorio ninkore ekerogo kiao ki'oborwoti kebe ne chinguru, buna nakorete okobwatana kw'ogotianania na Daudi iso, nkamoteebia: Omonto takobora korwa asore, oyio oragambere Abaisraeli.

English: and one third of the living creatures which were in the sea died. One third of the ships were destroyed.
Kiswahili: theluthi ya viumbe vyenye uhai viishivyo baharini vikafa na theluthi ya meli zikaharibiwa.
Ekegusii: Ensemo ya gatato y'enyancha ekaba amanyinga, na ensemo ya gatato y'ebitongwa bire moyo ime ase enyancha bigakwa, na ensemo ya gatato ye chimeeri chigasarigwa.

English: These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Kiswahili: Haya yalikuwa majina ya wana wa Lawi: Gershoni, Kohathi na Merari.
Ekegusii: Lawi nigo abwate abamura batato: Gerisoni, na Kohati, na Merari.

English: for he took away the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles,
Kiswahili: Akaziondoa madhabahu za kigeni na mahali pa juu pa kuabudia miungu, akayavunja yale mawe ya kuabudiwa na kuzikatakata nguzo za Maashera.
Ekegusii: Akarusia ebisasimero ebigeni na agasaria aase aimokererete igoro agosasimerwa, agatagora chisiiro, akanacha emete y'Asera, enyasae eria enkungu.

English: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.” Joseph Interprets Pharaoh’s Dreams
Kiswahili: Nayo mambo yakawa sawa kabisa na jinsi alivyotufasiria ndoto zetu: Mimi nilirudishwa kazini mwangu na huyo mtu mwingine akaangikwa.”
Ekegusii: Na buna ere atoteebetie engencho ye chindoto chiaito, naboigo abeete; inche nkairanigwa ase emeremo yane, na oria onde agasungwa ase omote igoro.”

English: One day Opio went out hunting with his dogs. After a short time, his dogs started to chase an antelope. Opio followed them. He ran for many hours. Every time he became tired, he rested. Then he would run again. But he could not find his dogs.
Kiswahili: Siku moja Opio alienda kuwinda na mbwa wake. Baada ya muda mfupi, mbwa waliona paa wakaanza kumfukuza. Opio aliwafuata. Alikimbia kwa masaa mengi. Kila alipochoka alipumzika na kisha kuanza kukimbia tena. Lakini hakuwaona mbwa wake.
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo Opio nigo arenge nomogoko omonene ekiagera nario ritang’ani riaye koinda ere bweka. Opio akarangeria chisese chiaye nakogenda koinda nachirochio. Ake igo chisese chiria chigachaka kominyokia engabi.

English: "The birds of the air will not laugh at us for being so low," said her friend. "We will not crawl, we will walk!" Very slowly the snakes uncoiled themselves. Close together they began to swim up, up, to the light above.
Kiswahili: “Ndege wa angani hawatatucheka na kutuona duni,” mwenzake alimjibu. “Hatutatambaa, tutatembea!” Nyoka hao walijikunjua polepole. Wakaanza kuogelea na kuogelea wakielekea juu kwenye mwangaza.
Ekegusii: Chinyoni chiria chikoiruruka tichigotosekerera kobera nse,” mosani oye agateba. “ekiagera titokouagura, nigo naintwe torabe togotara!” Ng’ora ng’ora hing’iti ciria chigachaka kweng’usororia. Chire amo ang’e ang’e cigachaka goaka ontimbu gochia ase oborabu boria igoro.

English: They never fought with each other. They helped their parents at home and in the fields.
Kiswahili: Hawakugombana hata kidogo. Watoto waliwasaidia wazazi nyumbani na shambani.
Ekegusii: Tibarenge korwana nonde bwensi. Nigo barenge gokonya abaibori babo nka sobo amo nase emegondo.

English: Where are you going? asked the young girl. Im going to visit my Uncle Mtonyama, said Nonkungu. Well, Mtonyama is my uncle, too and I am also on my way to visit him, said the young girl. So they walked on together.
Kiswahili: “Unaenda wapi?” Yule msichana alimwuliza. “Ninamtembelea mjombangu Mtonyama,” Nonkungu alisema. “Ala! Mtonyama ni mjombangu pia nami namtembelea,” yule msichana akasema. Wakatembea pamoja.
Ekegusii: “ing'ai ogochia” omoiseke oria akamoboria. “Nigo inkogenda komotarera tata moke Mtonyama,” Nokungu akamoiraneria. Ero bono, Mtonyama gose nainche tata moke, nainche noo ngochia komokwania,” omoiseke oria akamotebia.

English: During the weekend, Matata's children and their friends would climb uphill to play. They would run all over the place, breaking twigs and branches, lighting fires for their games, which they would later leave burning.
Kiswahili: Mwishoni mwa wiki, watoto wa Matata na marafiki zao wangepanda mlimani kucheza. Wangekimbia kila mahali huku wakivunja vijiti na matawi, wakiasha mioto kwa michezo yao ambayo baadaye, waliacha ikiwaka.
Ekegusii: Ekero Ki’Omokubio, abana ba’Matata amo nabasani babo nigo barenge korina egetunwa keria gochiesa. Nigo barenge kominyoka kera ase, bakobuna emete nechinsaginsagi, nagouta emerero barenge gotiga kegwoka. Engaki egaeta, Olokwango akagechiwa mono. Ng’ora ng’ora ogoseka koria kwaye kogachaka gosira. Chimboto chiria chiaye chigachaka gokea na gokea nobosio bwaye bogachaka konyira. Omoerio ndoche chiria ibere chigasira.

English: During the day Nonkungu went to the fields, hid in the corn, and sang: "Oh misery me, misery me. I was sent by my father and mother to stay with my Uncle Mtonyama. On the way I met an imbulu and she took my skirt and my beads. Oh misery me, misery me."
Kiswahili: Nonkungu aliimba: Matatizo matatizo! Wazazi walinituma, Kwa mjomba Mtonyama, Kakutana na imbulu, Nguo zangu kachukua, Matatizo matatizo!
Ekegusii: Mambia yaye Nokungu akagenda mogondo, akebisa ase chibando ime nagotera: “Gaki nche nachandekire, nachandkire. Ingatomwa na tata na mama ominto Kogenda komenya na tata moke Mtonyama. Nchera ginkogenda nkaumera Eimbulu akaira esikati yane

English: Once upon a time, there was a boy called Demane. He had a twin sister called Demazane.
Kiswahili: Hapo zamani za kale paliondokea mvulana mmoja aliyeitwa Demane. Alikuwa na pacha mwenzake aliyeitwa Demazane. Wazazi wao walipofariki, Demane na Demazane walienda kuishi na mjomba wao. Huko kwa mjomba wao, walitendewa mabaya. Walichapwa kwa vibiko virefu, na walipewa uji mwepesi mara moja tu kwa siku. Kwa sababu hiyo, walitoroka.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare omomura narenge ororo orenge korokwa Demane. Nigo abwate esare yambwabo orenge korokwa Demazana. Ekero abaibori babo bakwete nigo bachiete komenya na ise moke. Korende nigo bachandetwe mono. Nigo barenge goitwa nebiranya ebitambe, naboigo bakaba bakoegwa erongori yoka naende rimo rioka kera rituko. Igo bagatama.

English: One day the longing was too strong. His brothers warned him...
Kiswahili: Siku moja tamaa ya kwenda nje ikazidi. Wenzake wakamwonya asiende juani. Lakini, hakusikia.
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo okagania kwaye gokaba okonene. Bamura bamwabo bagachi komoonya ...

English: The wax children were so sad to see their brother melting away.
Kiswahili: Watoto wa nta walihuzunika walipoona kaka yao akiyeyuka.
Ekegusii: Abana baria ba amana bakaigwa bobe korora oyomwabo gakobera nakoera igo.

English: They were no longer snakes, but Man and Woman.
Kiswahili: Hawakuwa nyoka tena, kwani sasa waligeuka na kuwa mume na mke. Walitazamana na kupendana kama mume na mke.
Ekegusii: Korwa engaki eyio kogenderera bagatiga koba ching'iti, bono bakaba abanto, Omosacha nomokungu. Riria buna bakwenakwerigereria, baganchana.

English: "Come," said First Man. "I will," said First Woman. And they walked out together into their new world.
Kiswahili: “Hebu njoo,” Mume wa Kwanza alisema. “Naam,” akajibu Mke wa Kwanza. Kisha wakatembea pamoja kwenye ulimwengu wao mpya.
Ekegusii: “Inchwo,” omosacha oria omotang’ani “Nachire,” omokungu oria omotang’ani akairaneria Naende bagatara amo gochia ase ense eria yabo enyia.

English: On Tuesday I got a letter from my class.
Kiswahili: Siku ya Jumanne nilipokea barua kutoka kwa wanafunzi wa darasa langu.
Ekegusii: Etichi kabere inkanyora rirube korwa ase abana b’ekelasi kiane.

English: And as they reached the surface of the water, a strange thing happened. The tips of their tails split into two. They grew limbs with feet and toes. From just beneath their heads grew two arms with hands and fingers.
Kiswahili: Walipokaribia juu ya maji, maajabu yalitendeka. Mikia yao iligawika mara mbili wakawa na miguu yenye vidole. Na mikono miwili yenye vidole ilitokea chini ya vichwa vyao.
Ekegusii: Riria buna chigochia goika igoro y’amache aria, egento kiogokumia gekaba. Omoerio bw’emincha biabo bikabagana bikaba bibere – bikaba amagoro abwate ebiara. Na korwa nse yemetwe yabo, amaboko abere nebiara amo nenchinchara bikamera.

English: He called out to the hornets, "Hey hornets! Come see! It is raining! Quick - get inside my gourd and it will keep all of you dry." Hornets don't like to get wet, so they all flew into Anansi's gourd.
Kiswahili: Kisha akawaita manyigu, “Aisee manyigu! Njooni mwone! Mvua inanyesha! Haraka – ingieni ndani ya kibuyu changu ili mjikinge na mvua. Manyigu hawapendi kulowa maji; kwa hivyo, walikimbilia ndani ya kibuyu cha Anansi.
Ekegusii: Koruoo akarangeria ebiarambe biria, “inwe ebiarambe ebi! Inchwo morore! Embura yature! Bwango bwango soa igaa ase ekerandi kiane kebakenge korwa ase embura.” Momanyete ebiarambe tibiancheti gotwerwa, igo bikairuruka bigasoa ekerandi keria kia Anansi ime.

English: And that is how night came to Opio's village.
Kiswahili: Na hivyo ndivyo usiku ulivyoingia kijijini kwa kina Opio.
Ekegusii: Naigo nabo obotuko bwaigete ase ekenyoro ki’Opiyo.

English: Last week I received a lot of letters.
Kiswahili: Wiki iliyopita nilipokea barua nyingi.
Ekegusii: Ewiki eria yaeta inanyora amarube amange mono.

English: The giant then asked the girl loved by both parents to help her put a load of firewood on her back. So the girl followed the giant.
Kiswahili: Kisha jitu likamwambia msichana anayependwa na wazazi wote alifuate akalisaidie kuinua tita la kuni mgongoni. Kwa hivyo, msichana huyo alilifuata jitu.
Ekegusii: Richini riria koruoo rikaboria omoiseke oria bwanchire n’abaibori baye bonsi amokonye komotweka chinko mogongo oye. Omoiseke oria akabwatia richini riria.

English: Soon the snake came out and asked what the argument was. I was arguing with my wife, said Anansi. She says this stick is longer than you are. But I dont agree. Of course Im longer than that stick! said the snake. Im very long! Im a huge snake! Just put your stick next to me and measure!
Kiswahili: Mara nyoka akatokea kwenye maji akawauliza sababu ya mabishano yao. “Mke wangu anasema kwamba kijiti hiki ni kirefu kuliko wewe,” Anansi alisema. “Lakini mimi sikubaliani naye.” “Lakini ni wazi kwamba mimi ni mrefu kuliko kijiti hicho!” nyoka alisema. “Mimi ni nyoka mrefu sana! Hebu weka kijiti karibu nami nijipime.”
Ekegusii: Ake igo, eng'iti eria egasoka na kobaboria ninki barenge koamererania. “Nigo narenge koamererania namokane oyo, “ Anansi agateba, “Okoba agoteba buna egete eke negetambe gokobua. Rakini tinyancheraneti.” Ayio namaene inche nomotambe nde kobua egete ekio!” eng'iti erai ekabatebia. “nche nomotamber mono! Nigo inde omonene mono! Beka ango egete ekio ang'e nainche monyare gopima!”

English: Opio did as he was told. That evening, he began to walk towards his village. He felt the dark night behind him as he walked. He wanted to look back. But he did not.
Kiswahili: Opio alifanya alivyoambiwa. Usiku huo alianza kutembea akielekea kijijini kwao. Alisikia giza la usiku likimfuata nyuma yake. Alitaka kuangalia nyuma lakini hakuangalia.
Ekegusii: Opio agakora buna atebetigwe. Agachaka koirana ekenyoro kiaye emarogoba eria yarenge kobwatia. Akagania korigereria magega. Korende tarigerereti. Akanya gosuka ang'e n'ekenyoro kiaye. Ake ake agachaka korora ekenyoro kiaye nabasani baye.

English: How much do the stories cost? asked Anansi. Youll have to bring me three rare and fierce animals, Nyame answered, A leopard with sharp teeth like spears, a hornet that stings people, and a snake that swallows people whole. He laughed and laughed. He thought his stories were quite safe.
Kiswahili: “Hadithi hugharimu pesa ngapi?” Anansi aliuliza.” “Itabidi uniletee wanyama watatu wakali na wa kipekee”, Nyamae alijibu, “chui mwenye meno makali kama mkuki, nyigu anayewauma watu, na nyoka anayewameza watu.” Alicheka na kucheka. Alidhani kwamba hadithi zake zilikuwa salama.
Ekegusii: “Nechibesa irenga emegano eye eragorwe?” Anansi akaboria. “Goika ondetere emenyama etatu emiya naende emekari,” Nyame akamoiraneria, “echui eria ebwate amaino amoge buna amatimo, ekiarambe keria gekorasa abanto, ne'ng'iti eria ekomera abanto abagima. Agaseka naende agaseka mbaka amaiso aye akarwa amariga. Akarengereria buna emegano eria nigo yagachire buya mono.

English: When the man heard what the girl sang, he rescued her and took her back to her parents. The story ends there!
Kiswahili: Mwanamume huyo aliposikia wimbo wa msichana alimnusuru kutoka kwa jitu na kumrudisha kwa wazazi wake. Hadithi inaishia hapo!
Ekegusii: Ekero omosacha oria aigwete amang'ana y'ogotera koria, akamotoria nakomoirania ase abaibori baye. Noo omogano one oererete abwo!

English: It was a very hot Saturday afternoon in December.
Kiswahili: Ilikuwa Jumamosi moja iliyokuwa na joto jingi sana katika mwezi wa Desemba. Kila mtu alikuwa amenuna. “Bontle na Mpho na Lerato, nendeni nje mcheze!” Mama alitwambia. “Siwataki miguuni mwangu.”
Ekegusii: Nigo riberera riarenge igoro sana omokubio oyomo omotienyi oikomi nakabere Kera omonto nigo arenge konya kwemurungania. Bontle na Mpho na Lerato, soka isiko mochiese Mme agatotebia. Timbatageti igaa ase amagoro ane.

English: They walked on and met a man. He asked the giant, "What is the name of your child?" The giant replied, "She is called the 'talking bag'."
Kiswahili: Waliendelea kutembea. Wakakutana na mwanamume. Mwanamume akaliuliza jitu, “Huyu mtoto wako anaitwaje?” Jitu likajibu, “Anaitwa Mfuko Uzunguzao.”
Ekegusii: Kobagendererete kogenda, bakaumerana n’omosacha oyomo. Omosacha oria akaboria richini riria ng’a, “Inaki omwana oyo oo akorokwa?” Richini riria rikamoiraneria buna, “nigo akorokwa ‘Omobuko ogokwana.”

English: Each evening Demane brought back something he had killed – a hare or some birds or a small buck. As he came to the cave, he sang, Demazane, Demazane, child of my mother, open this cave to me. The swallows can enter it. It has two holes.
Kiswahili: Demazane alichoka sana kukaa pangoni peke yake. Basi siku moja kakake alipoondoka, naye Demazane alitoka na kwenda matembezi. Aliona mto mdogo akaogelea kwa furaha sana. Pia alipanda miti akaendelea kustarehe. Alifurahia uhuru wa kucheza. “Labda hakuna majitu,” aliwaza. “Pengine mjomba alisema kuna majitu ili kututisha tu.”
Ekegusii: Demazane akarosa kobera ere bweka ase ekerongo keria kera rituko. Igo rituko erimo, ekero momura omwabo asogete isiko gochia koinda na gotega emenyama, agasoka nere korora. Akanyora oroche agasoa ime gochiesa, na korina emete igoro. Akaigwa buya koba isiko ye'kerongo keria. “Oranyore,” banto tibaiyo bakoria abande. Gose onyore buna tata moke nigo arenge gototebia igo erinde tooboe.”

English: So Anansi did that, and he tied the snake to the stick with his vine to keep him straight. When he was all tied up, Anansi took the snake up to heaven.
Kiswahili: Anansi alifanya hivyo. Kisha akamfunga yule nyoka kwenye kijiti kile kwa kutumia kamba ili kumnyoosha sawasawa. Baada ya kumfunga huyo nyoka vizuri, alimbeba hadi juu mbinguni.
Ekegusii: Igo anansi agakora igo nagosiba eng’iti eria nomogoye oria erinde eng’iti eria enyare koramboka kabisa ase egete keria. Ekero akorete gosiba eng’iti eria nemegoye eria, anansi akayebogoria akayeira mbaka igoro onyasae.

English: On the way Nonkungu came to a stream. She crossed the stream using the stepping stones. On the other side she met a young girl wearing rags.
Kiswahili: Nonkungu alivuka mto na kukutana na msichana aliyevaa matambara.
Ekegusii: Nchera gakogenda akaumerana noroche. Agatamboka oroche roria kagotacha amagena arengeoo. Ase eng'umbu eria yende akaumerana nomoiseke oyomo obegete chiyanga amachanchabe.

English: Long ago, there was no night in Opios village. People slept when they were tired and worked when they were awake.
Kiswahili: Hapo zamani za kale hapakuwa na usiku katika kijiji cha kina Opio. Watu walilala wakati wowote ule waliposikia uchovu. Walifanya kazi walipokuwa hawajalala.
Ekegusii: Kare sana, botuko mbwarengeoo ase ekenyoro kia Opio. Abanto nigo barenge korara kobarosire nagokora egasi ekero babogete.

English: When they reached the tree, Nonkungu said to the imbulu, "Please give me back my skirt and beads." "Just let me wear them until we get to the next stream," said the imbulu. Nonkungu was afraid, so she agreed.
Kiswahili: Baadaye, Nonkungu alimwambia Imbulu tena, “Tafadhali nirudishie rinda na mkufu wangu.” Hata hivyo, Imbulu hakumpatia.
Ekegusii: Ekero baigete ase omote oria, Nonkungu agatebia Eimbulu eria, “Gaki ing’a esikati yane amo n’erindere riane.” “Tiga aye mbibeke baka toike ase oroche ronde rore bosio bwaito, Eimbulu eria ekamotebia. Nonkungu akaba nobwoba obonge, igo agancherana tu.

English: He called out to the hornets, Hey hornets! Come see! It is raining! Quick - get inside my gourd and it will keep all of you dry. Hornets dont like to get wet, so they all flew into Anansis gourd.
Kiswahili: Kisha akawaita manyigu, “Aisee manyigu! Njooni mwone! Mvua inanyesha! Haraka – ingieni ndani ya kibuyu changu ili mjikinge na mvua. Manyigu hawapendi kulowa maji; kwa hivyo, walikimbilia ndani ya kibuyu cha Anansi.
Ekegusii: Koruoo akarangeria ebiarambe biria, “inwe ebiarambe ebi! Inchwo morore! Embura yature! Bwango bwango soa igaa ase ekerandi kiane kebakenge korwa ase embura.” Momanyete ebiarambe tibiancheti gotwerwa, igo bikairuruka bigasoa ekerandi keria kia Anansi ime.

English: And as they reached the surface of the water, a strange thing happened. The tips of their tails split into two. They grew limbs with feet and toes. From just beneath their heads grew two arms with hands and fingers.
Kiswahili: Walipokaribia juu ya maji, maajabu yalitendeka. Mikia yao iligawika mara mbili wakawa na miguu yenye vidole. Na mikono miwili yenye vidole ilitokea chini ya vichwa vyao.
Ekegusii: Riria buna chigochia goika igoro y'amache aria, egento kiogokumia gekaba. Omoerio bw'emincha biabo bikabagana bikaba bibere – bikaba amagoro abwate ebiara. Na korwa nse yemetwe yabo, amaboko abere nebiara amo nenchinchara bikamera.

English: Khayanga held the pieces of the broken Gourd in her small hands and sang: Father and Mother, See the gourd is broken. The gourd you gave me. What do I do, Mother and Father? Be kind and show me a sign... That you are still with me.
Kiswahili: Khayanga alivishika vigae vya Kibuyu kilichovunjika mikononi mwake akaimba: Baba yangu mama yangu Kibuyu mlichonipa, Jamani kimevunjika. Nieleze nifanyeje? Baba yangu mama yangu, Nipe ishara nyingine, Nijue mko na mimi.
Ekegusii: Khayanga held the pieces of the broken Gourd in her small hands and sang: Father and Mother, See the gourd is broken. The gourd you gave me. What do I do, Mother and Father? Be kind and show me a sign... That you are still with me.

English: Then the imbulu went to Uncle Mtonyama's hut. She said sweetly, "I am your niece, Nonkungu. My parents sent me to stay with you." Mtonyama welcomed the young girl. He and his family were very kind to the imbulu. But poor Nonkungu had to sleep in the kraal and share the dog's food.
Kiswahili: Imbulu alimwambia Mtonyama, “Mimi ni mpwa wako, Nonkungu. Wazazi wamenituma niishi nawe." Walimfurahia sana huku Nonkungu akilala nje.
Ekegusii: Koruoo Eimbulu eria ekagenda nyomba mwa Isemoke Mtonyama nakomotebia, “Ninche moigwa oo, Nokungu. Abaobori bane nigo bantoma komenya naye.” Mtonyama akaarigania omoiseke oria nyomba. Ere nenka yaye bakaba abororo ase eimbulu eria. Rakini Nokungu akarara

English: Mtonyama had heard that an imbulu's tail loves milk and that it can't go past milk without drinking some. So he told his men to dig a deep ditch and to fill the ditch with sour milk. Then he called all the girls of the village to take part in a jumping competition.
Kiswahili: Mtonyama alisikia kwamba mkia wa Imbulu ulipenda kunywa maziwa. Wafanyi kazi wake walichimba shimo wakalijaza maziwa. Wasichana wote kijijini walishindana kuruka.
Ekegusii: Mtonyama konyora oigure buna ekemincha k’ieimbulu nigo gianchete amabere naende tikegoetania mabere getaranywa nonya namake igo. Igo agatebia abamura baye bareme engoro nakoyeichoria n’amabere amaruranu. Erinde akabarangeria abaiseke bonsi bekenyoro basindane

English: One day her parents decided to send her to stay with her rich Uncle Mtonyama. Nonkungu's mother made a special skirt with ribbon, buttons and beads. She also made a beautiful bead necklace for Nonkungu. Then she sent her off to her uncle's village.
Kiswahili: Siku moja wazazi walimtuma Nonkungu akaishi na mjombake tajiri. Mamake alimtengenezea Nonkungu mkufu wa shanga na rinda alilolirembesha kwa shanga.
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo, abaibori baye bakaamua komotoma gochia komenya na Ise moke orenge etachiri naende orenge korokwa Mtonyama. Ng’ina Nonkungu akamoroseria esikati yabwate emengori, ebibungo amo namaritati ande. Naende akamoroseria rindere ri’ebigoti.

English: Long long ago people didnt know anything. They didnt know how to plant crops, or how to weave cloth, or how to make iron tools. The god Nyame up in the sky had all the wisdom of the world. He kept it safe in a clay pot.
Kiswahili: Hapo zamani za kale, watu hawakujua chochote. Hawakujua kupanda mimea, hawakujua kushona nguo, wala hawakujua kuunda zana za chuma. Nyame, mungu aliyekuwa mbinguni, ndiye aliyekuwa mwenye hekima zote za dunia. Alihifadhi hekima hiyo kwenye chungu cha udongo.
Ekegusii: Igabwo kare kare banto tibamanyete kende. Tibamanyete gosimeka endagera, gose gosona yanga, gose korosia ebinto korua ase chichuma. Nonya nigo nyasaye orenge korokwa Nyame narengeoo gotatiga amenyete igoro ase rise naende nigo abwate obong'aini bwensi bwense. Nigo agachete obong'aini obo ase enyongo.

English: Khayanga heard her mothers voice saying to her: Our child, pick up the pieces that are left. Fetch water with them and wash your feet. When you finish washing, close your eyes. Khayanga obeyed and suddenly, the broken Gourd became whole once again.
Kiswahili: Khayanga akasikia sauti ya mamake ikimwambia: Khayanga mtoto wetu, Hivyo vigae okota, Na maji uchote navyo, Ioshe miguu yako, Ukimaliza kuosha, Uyafunge macho yako. Khayanga alitii alivyoambiwa na ghafla, Kibuyu kilichovunjika kilishikana tena. Alikichukua akakishika kifuani mwake kwa furaha kubwa.
Ekegusii: Khayanga heard her mother's voice saying to her: Our child, pick up the pieces that are left. Fetch water with them and wash your feet. When you finish washing, close your eyes. Khayanga obeyed and suddenly, the broken Gourd became whole once again.

English: Long long ago when the earth was new, great mountains covered the world like a blanket, and tall trees spiked the sky.
Kiswahili: Hapo zamani za kale dunia ilipokuwa mpya, milima mikubwa ilifunika ulimwengu kama blanketi. Nayo miti mirefu ilichongoka mawinguni.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare ekero riroba riarenge rinyia, ebitunwa ebinge nigo biatubete ense eye buna oborangeti, nemete emetambe nigo yabetete erioba.

English: Thabisile is sick. She must stay at home.
Kiswahili: Thabisile ni mgonjwa. Ni lazima akae nyumbani.
Ekegusii: Thabisile nomorwaire. Goika atigare nka.

English: Anansi spun a long thread, and climbed up his sticky thread all the way to heaven. "Can I have the stories, please?" he asked the Sky God. But Nyame laughed at Anansi and said, "Oh, these are very expensive stories. You wouldn't be able to pay for them, little spider."
Kiswahili: Anansi alisokota utando mrefu unaonata, akautumia kupanda hadi mbinguni. “Tafadhali nipe hadithi?” Anansi alimwambia Mungu wa Mbinguni. Lakini Nyamae alimcheka Anansi akisema, “Hadithi hizi ni ghali mno. Hutaweza kuzilipia, buibui mdogo, wee.”
Ekegusii: Anansi, akarosia eusi etaambe nakorina eusi eria yarenge konanta mbaka igoro o’nyasae. “Ninyore emegano aria, gaki?” akaboria Nyasae Bwe’rioba. Rakini Nyame akamosekerera kagoteba, “ Obe, emegano eye nigo ere yerigori rinene. Tokonyara koyeakanera aye, akanyambobe aka.”

English: "Oh let me help you, my dear friend!" said Anansi. "Just lie down on these sticks and I'll pull you out." Anansi wound his sticky web round the leopard and the sticks, and pulled him up to heaven to show the Sky God. But Nyame just laughed and said, "Where are the other two?"
Kiswahili: “Hebu nikusaidie, rafiki yangu.” Anansi alisema.” “Hebu lalia vijiti hivi halafu nitakuvuta nje.” Anansi akautungia utando wake unaonata, kwa mwili wa chui, na vijiti, kisha akamvuta hadi juu kwa Mungu wa Mbinguni. Lakini, Nyamae alimcheka akauliza, “Wale wengine wawili wako wapi?”
Ekegusii: Obe gaki, tiga inkokonye, mosani one!” Anansi agateba. “Rara inse igaiga ase ebite ebi erinde inyare gokongusa koru engoro eyio ime.” Korwa aroro Anansi agachaka gosiba echui eria neusi yaye amo nebite, nakomokurura mbaka igoro ase rire gochia komwoorokia Nyasae. Rakini Nyame agaseka tu nakomoboria, “Ng’ai emenyama eria yende ere?

English: One day, Nyame decided that he would give the pot of wisdom to Anansi. Every time Anansi looked in the clay pot, he learned something new. It was so exciting!
Kiswahili: Siku moja, Nyame aliamua kumpa Anansi chungu hicho cha hekima. Kila Anansi alipotazama ndani ya chungu cha udongo, alijifunza jambo jipya. Alifurahi sana!
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo, Nyame akaamua koenana enyongo eria y’obong’aini gosia ase Anansi. Kera engaki Anansi arigereretie enyongo eria, nigo arenge kweegeria egento ekeyia. Nero nigo yare komorentera omogoko omonge.

English: For ages, Olokwango hill stood smiling at the middle of Kwere plains. From the two dimples on its side came springs which converged downhill to form a river. River Temu meandered silently across the Kwere plains. Its waters were a gift to the sheep and goats of the area as well as the deer that dwelt in the plains.
Kiswahili: Kwa muda mrefu mlima wa Olokwango ulisimama ukitabasamu katikati ya sehemu Tambarare ya Kwere. Kutoka kwa vibonyeo viwili vilivyokuwa pembeni mwa mlima huo, kulitoka vijito vilivyokaribiana na kutengeza mto.
Ekegusii: Ase emiaka emenge, egetunwa ki’Olokwango nigo giatenenete kegoseka gatigati y’eroro y’Akwere. Korwa ase chimboto na ase ensemo yaye chinsoko ibere inchiarwete aroro nakoumerana korosia oroche oronene oromo.
